title: Shop rentals in heritage precincts and support for heritage businesses
asked: MPs asked what measures the Ministry is taking to moderate shop rentals in heritage precincts such as Chinatown and Kampong Gelam to support long-standing heritage businesses, and whether the Government is aware of bidding wars and subletting driving up rents in Kampong Gelam and will act to curb them.
asked_by: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng and Mr Fadli Fawzi
response: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi said the Government monitors retail rents and that URA data shows median rents in Kampong Gelam, Little India and Chinatown rose about 2% per annum over the past two years, comparable to Central Area conventional retail and below nominal GDP growth. He said the reported closure of Warong Nasi Pariaman was not rental-related, agencies are in touch about possible continuation, and support continues through the Inter-Agency Task Force and the SG Heritage Business Scheme. On supplementaries, he said there are no current plans for ABSD/SSD or property tax changes for commercial property, Wakaf-land shophouses are outside the remit of this set of questions, and URA controls exclude non-heritage users from core historic districts.

key_points.point: The Government monitors retail rents across Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: The Government carefully monitors retail rents across Singapore.

key_points.point: URA data shows median rents in Kampong Gelam, Little India and Chinatown, including sublet arrangements, rose about 2% per annum over the past two years.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: median rents for retail spaces in historic districts of Kampong Gelam, Little India and Chinatown, including sublet arrangements, have increased at a moderate pace of around 2% per annum over the past two years

key_points.point: Those increases were comparable to conventional retail space in the Central Area and lower than nominal GDP growth.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: These increases were comparable with rental increases of conventional retail space in the Central Area and lower than nominal gross domestic product (GDP) growth over the same period.

key_points.point: The reported closure of Warong Nasi Pariaman was not related to rental issues.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: the closure was not related to rental issues

key_points.point: Agencies are in touch with Warong Nasi Pariaman about facilitating its continuation if the family decides to do so.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: the agencies are in touch with Warong Nasi Pariaman to discuss how we can facilitate their continuation should they decide to do so

key_points.point: Support includes marketing and business consultancy under NHB's SG Heritage Business Scheme.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: marketing and business consultancy support under the National Heritage Board's (NHB's) SG Heritage Business Scheme

key_points.point: URA's rental data comes from comprehensive rental records submitted for stamp duty purposes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: This is based on comprehensive rental records submitted for the stamp duty purposes.

key_points.point: A small proportion of leases signed between 2023 and 2025 saw increases of 25% or higher.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: there was also a small proportion of leases signed between 2023 and 2025 which did see higher rental increases of 25% or higher

key_points.point: Even with increases, rents remained around 20% to 60% below conventional retail spaces in the Central Area as a whole.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: their rental rates remained around 20% to 60% below that of conventional retail spaces in the Central Area as a whole

key_points.point: In October 2025, NHB launched the SG Heritage Business Scheme to recognise heritage businesses and encourage public appreciation of their cultural value.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: In October 2025, NHB launched the SG Heritage Business Scheme to recognise heritage businesses and encourage public appreciation of their cultural value.

key_points.point: 42 businesses have been designated under the scheme, including 21 in Kampong Gelam and Chinatown.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Today, 42 businesses have been designated under the scheme, including 21 in Kampong Gelam and Chinatown.

key_points.point: There are no current plans for ABSD or property tax changes for commercial property.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: there are no current plans that the Ministry has with regard to these two steps

key_points.point: Wakaf-land shophouses in Kampong Gelam are outside the remit of this set of questions.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: I believe that is not within the remit of the questions that I will be answering for this set of Parliamentary Questions.

key_points.point: URA controls exclude non-heritage users such as fast food restaurants, supermarkets and new bars from core historic districts.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: the URA has put in place controls to exclude non-heritage users, such as fast food restaurants, supermarkets and new bars

key_points.point: Partnerships include the upcoming Ramadan bazaar between URA and Kampong Gelam Alliance.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: the upcoming Ramadan bazaar between URA as well as Kampong Gelam Alliance

key_points.point: The Ministry will partner alliances and stakeholders to find the most suitable outcome for businesses.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: we will be looking towards wanting to partner the different alliances and the different stakeholders to be able to find the most suitable outcome moving forward for our businesses

left_open: Any action specifically to curb bidding wars and subletting in Kampong Gelam.
A specific timeline for coordination among MND, MTI, NAC, NHB and URA.
The criteria for what qualifies as a heritage business.
Whether conservation and place management could incorporate business incubation and structured tenant mix for younger businesses.
Whether SME Centres will be involved in identifying non-rental, rental or manpower issues for heritage businesses.
Plans to work with Warees Investments on Wakaf-land shophouses in Kampong Gelam.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered rental data sources, agency coordination, stamp duties and property tax, Wakaf land, planning controls, tenant mix and support for heritage SMEs.
